image.subject: an old paper property deed lying on a dark wooden table beside a heavy iron house key, one lamp lit beside them

storyboard.claim: Owning a home is assumed to mean holding the deed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A deed and a key on a table, the ownership papers the narrator says everyone trusts.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the video with the common assumption.
storyboard.addedInformation: The deed is the paper that is supposed to prove ownership.

storyboard.claim: Ordinary homeowner life is a mortgage and small decorating choices.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-item list of the mortgage and the paint colours.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists what the narrator means by believing you own the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mortgage payments and decorating are the everyday signs of feeling in control.

image.subject: a seventeenth-century timber house with a steep grey roof and small leaded windows under a heavy New England sky, no people in view

storyboard.claim: A very old house has more power over its residents than they have over it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A 350-year-old timber house looming under a grey sky.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the homeowner's view to the house's view.
storyboard.addedInformation: The house is the estate Peton, shown as the centre of the story.

image.subject: the damp stone and brick cellar wall of an old house, a wooden door ajar and warm lantern light on worn stone steps, no people

storyboard.claim: The house decides who lives and where the dead are put.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cellar of old brick and stone with a shovel and loose earth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the house's power in concrete terms.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shovel and loose earth show the burying the narrator describes.

storyboard.claim: Wood and brick last longer than people do, which is the grim truth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A text card with the one line about how long wood and brick last.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A short aside after the claim about burial.
storyboard.addedInformation: Explains why the house outlasts the people who live in it.

storyboard.claim: The house survives civil wars, famines and the industrial revolution.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A timeline card listing the wars, famines and industrial change the house outlived.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Widens the view from one building to centuries of history.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the house as a survivor across many eras.

image.subject: a dim wood-panelled hallway with an old oil portrait of a stern family in dark clothing hanging above a carved chest

storyboard.claim: Generations of one family rise and fall inside the house, and the cause is the people inside it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An old family portrait in a dim panelled hall above a carved chest.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the house to the family living in it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Suggests the family itself, not maintenance, keeps the house standing.

left.label: POURED STONE
left.subject: a clean new stone foundation in a neat trench, bright and freshly laid

right.label: COMPROMISE
right.subject: the same trench with dark earth packed against the stone and an old pale bone half-buried in it

storyboard.claim: A legacy estate is built on a compromise with the ground, not on clean stone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two side-by-side views: a clean foundation, then the same foundation over buried earth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the bargain a visual form.
storyboard.addedInformation: The second side shows what the compromise hides under the foundation.

image.subject: a worn paperback novel with a dark cover lying on a dusty wooden table, the cover showing a black silhouette of a house behind bare trees

storyboard.claim: The Witch looks like a supernatural story from its cover.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A paperback with a dark cover showing a house silhouette.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the book the video is about.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cover shows the ghost-story look the narrator says is a disguise.

image.subject: a narrow dirt road winding through dense woods toward a lone grey house, low fog over the grass at dusk, no people

storyboard.claim: The book reads like a creepy isolated ghost story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dirt road into dense woods toward one lonely house in fog.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Expands the cover into the book's surface genre.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the isolated setting that the ghost-story reading depends on.

image.subject: a lantern held up in a dark wood at night, its light on old bare tree trunks and a worn wooden floorboard at a doorway

storyboard.claim: Beneath the ghost story are real Massachusetts witch trials, and the narrator will look under the floorboards.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lantern in a dark wood and a worn floorboard at a doorway.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the ghost-story surface to what lies beneath it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Links the floorboards to the Massachusetts trials.

storyboard.claim: The book is a thriller about inheritance, not a ghost story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A text card stating the thriller about inheritance claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the real genre directly after the disguise.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names inheritance as the theme of the whole argument.

image.subject: the heavy chestnut front door of a seventeenth-century timber house, with an iron bear-head knocker, shut tight, no people

storyboard.claim: The estate Peton is the real protagonist and the real monster.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A closed chestnut front door with an iron bear-head knocker.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the estate as the central character.
storyboard.addedInformation: The iron knocker stands for the house as a shield.

left.subject: Caroline: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, standing by a candlelit window

right.label: PRESENT DAY
right.subject: Julia: a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, standing by a dim window in the same house

storyboard.claim: The 1692 and present-day timelines ask the same question.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two women in the same house, one in period dress and one in modern clothes, by windows.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pairs the two timelines the narrator names.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the two women as two eras of one story.

storyboard.claim: What is the family willing to bury on its own land to keep its house?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A text card with the question as the only content.
storyboard.onScreenText: What is the family willing to bury on their own property to keep their house?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The shared question of both timelines, stated outright.
storyboard.addedInformation: Defines the central moral question of the book.

image.subject: an old hand-drawn architect's floor plan of a timber house on yellowed paper, pencil room lines and a compass rose, laid flat on a table

storyboard.claim: The narrator will go through the board of the house layout to find the trap.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A yellowed floor plan of a timber house on a table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the question into a plan of the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: The plan is the layout the trap is built into.

image.subject: Julia: a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, sitting on the bare floor of an empty apartment beside one cardboard box

storyboard.claim: Julia Barlo is 27 and the present-day protagonist.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia sits alone on a bare apartment floor with a single box.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the present-day protagonist after the setup.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her age and emptiness set up her financial need.

image.subject: Julia: a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, sitting at a bare table with unopened envelopes spread in front of her

storyboard.claim: Julia is broke and at the lowest point of her adult life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia at a bare table with unopened envelopes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows her situation as she is introduced.
storyboard.addedInformation: Unopened envelopes show money pressure.

image.subject: an empty classroom with chairs stacked on small desks and a closed notice on the door, grey afternoon light

storyboard.claim: Her nonprofit tutoring job ended when its funding was cut.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty classroom with chairs stacked on desks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the first cause of her money trouble.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stacked chairs show the program has closed.

image.subject: a bare city apartment with bare walls, stacked moving boxes and a window over a busy street at dusk

storyboard.claim: She lost her Manhattan apartment in one of the most expensive cities.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stacked boxes in an empty apartment with a city window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the second cause, the housing loss.
storyboard.addedInformation: Boxes in an empty flat show she has already moved out.

image.subject: a close-up of Julia: a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair with one distinct white streak at the temple, tired expression

storyboard.claim: Julia has a white patch in her hair, a sign of stress or genetics.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A close-up of Julia's dark hair with a white streak at the temple.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives Julia a visible mark of her strain.
storyboard.addedInformation: The patch is the physical marker the narrator mentions.

image.subject: a single worn duffel bag and a cardboard box on a dim city sidewalk beside a closed shopfront

storyboard.claim: Julia is adrift with nowhere to go and only her belongings.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A duffel bag and a cardboard box on a sidewalk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows her belongings packed before the move.
storyboard.addedInformation: Only a few bags show how little she has.

image.subject: a rural New England dirt drive leading through dense woods to a grey seventeenth-century timber house, afternoon light, no people

storyboard.claim: Julia moves to the Peton estate in the wooded town of Wood Haven.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dirt drive through dense woods to a grey timber house.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows where she moves after the sidewalk.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the house in a rural, wooded town.

image.subject: an empty armchair beside a narrow bed with a folded quilt, a window with thin grey light, a shawl over the chair arm

storyboard.claim: Her grandmother Letty, 85, is slipping into a fog of age.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty armchair and a made bed in a grey room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the reason Julia moved in.
storyboard.addedInformation: The empty chair stands for a relative who is fading.

image.subject: Ethel: an elderly woman in her eighties, thin, grey hair in a bun, dark cardigan, stern face, standing at a kitchen sink with her arms folded

storyboard.claim: Ethel is sharp and runs the household with an iron grip.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ethel standing with folded arms at a kitchen sink.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the second relative who controls the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her stance shows her control of the household.

storyboard.claim: Ethel is terrifying.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A text card with the one word judgement on Ethel.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A short reaction to the previous portrait.
storyboard.addedInformation: Confirms the tone of the Ethel description.

image.subject: an overgrown backyard of tall grass and tangled brush behind a timber house, late afternoon, no people

storyboard.claim: The backyard is wild, not a manicured lawn.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tall grass and tangled brush behind an old house.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves the story outside to the catalyst.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the wild yard that hides the bone.

image.subject: Julia: a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, crouching on a back porch step and looking down at the dark soil of a wild overgrown yard

storyboard.claim: Julia looks down at the dirt in the wild backyard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia crouching on a porch step looking into dark soil.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts Julia into the backyard setting.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her crouch shows she is noticing something in the soil.

image.subject: a weathered pale bone, a human pelvis, half-exposed in dark soil at the roots of a tree, no body visible

storyboard.claim: What she finds is a 300-year-old human pelvic bone, not a deer bone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A weathered pale pelvic bone half out of dark soil.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reveals the object she finds.
storyboard.addedInformation: The bone is human, which changes the story.

image.subject: a coarse hemp rope lying across dark wet soil beside a pale bone edge, roots around them

storyboard.claim: The bone is a tether that pulls the story back to 1692.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A hemp rope across soil next to the pale bone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the bone into the link to the past.
storyboard.addedInformation: The rope is the image of the pull toward 1692.

image.subject: Caroline: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, standing in a wood-panelled room lit by candles

storyboard.claim: Caroline Eldridge is a young second wife in 1692.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline standing in a candlelit panelled room in period dress.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Jumps the timeline back to 1692.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the 1692 protagonist.

image.subject: Archie Eldridge: a man in his fifties, heavy build, dark wool coat, white collar, stern face, standing in front of a seventeenth-century timber house

storyboard.claim: Archie Eldridge is a wealthy, powerful merchant and Caroline's husband.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Archie in a dark wool coat before the timber house.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces her husband after her.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows his status and the house he owns.

image.subject: a narrow 1692 village street of timber houses, a few townsfolk in dark period clothes gathered near a meeting house door, grey dusk light

storyboard.claim: The village of Wood Haven is sinking into paranoia.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A village street with townsfolk gathered near a meeting house.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the village around the estate.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the paranoid village around the Eldridge house.

image.subject: a narrow village lane at dusk, townsfolk in dark period clothes standing close together and turning away from one another

storyboard.claim: Neighbours turn on each other during the witch trials.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Townsfolk in a village lane turning away from one another.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the hysteria the village is in.
storyboard.addedInformation: The turned backs show neighbours turning against each other.

image.subject: a dark wooded estate edge at night, bare trees and low fog, a single faint lantern far off, no figure

storyboard.claim: A serial killer known as the Night Reaper hunts the town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dark wooded edge at night with one faint light.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds a real threat on top of the witch panic.
storyboard.addedInformation: The woods are where the killer is said to hunt.

image.subject: a dark forest path at night, a scrap of grey cloth caught on a low branch beside the wet mud, no figure

storyboard.claim: Jonas Reeve stalks the woods as a real killer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A forest path at night with a scrap of cloth on a branch.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the killer from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cloth is a trace of the hunt, without showing harm.

left.label: SUPERNATURAL
left.subject: a single candle burning in a dark cottage window, long shadows across the wall

right.label: REAL KILLER
right.subject: a muddy footprint on a forest path at night, the ground wet under bare trees

storyboard.claim: Supernatural panic is layered on top of a real serial killer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A candle in a dark window beside a muddy footprint on a forest path.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pairs the ghost threat with the human one.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows two kinds of threat in one frame.

image.subject: an old wooden barrel of black powder beside a sheet of brittle paper in dim candlelight

storyboard.claim: The village is a powder keg of fear.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A barrel of black powder beside a sheet of paper in candlelight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the danger a single explosive image.
storyboard.addedInformation: The barrel stands for the tension the narrator names.

image.subject: an old floorboard lifted up in a dim room, packed dark earth showing in the gap beneath it

storyboard.claim: The pressure forces old secrets up to the present day.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lifted floorboard with dark earth beneath.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the powder keg into secrets coming up.
storyboard.addedInformation: The lifted board shows buried things rising to the surface.

image.subject: a dim museum gallery with empty glass display cases and a single brass plaque, no people

storyboard.claim: Henry Ziegler is an ambitious curator from the Wood Haven Museum.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Henry in a tweed jacket in a museum gallery beside display cases.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the next present-day character.
storyboard.addedInformation: His museum role sets up the offer for the house.

image.subject: a polished empty desk in a museum office with a thick cream document folder lying on it, no people

storyboard.claim: Henry makes a generous offer to buy Peton and keep it as a historical site.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Henry pushes a contract across a desk toward the reader, leaning in with a polite but intense look.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the buyer behind the tension.
storyboard.addedInformation: The buyer is a museum curator making a large offer.

image.subject: an old wooden kitchen table covered in unpaid bills and unopened envelopes, a single lamp lit in a dim farmhouse kitchen

storyboard.claim: The offer is a financial lifeline for a family that is broke.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A table buried under bills, lamp light, nobody at it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The offer is good on paper; now the costs.
storyboard.addedInformation: The family is financially desperate.

image.subject: orange survey stakes and string lines marking a grid across a dead-grass lawn in front of a seventeenth-century timber house, overcast sky

storyboard.claim: The tension comes from the excavation the museum would start.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Survey stakes and string laid across the lawn, marking where digging would happen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the money to the threat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Digging would start on the estate grounds.

image.subject: a yellow excavator with its bucket raised, parked on the lawn beside an old timber house in daylight

storyboard.claim: If the museum buys the estate, heavy machinery will come in.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A yellow excavator parked at the edge of the old house.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the survey stakes into an actual machine.
storyboard.addedInformation: Heavy machinery is part of the purchase plan.

image.subject: a freshly graded gravel field being laid as a parking lot, with a timber house standing at its far edge

storyboard.claim: The museum would dig to build parking lots and visitor exhibits.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A raw field turned into a parking lot, the old house in the distance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Says what the machines would be for.
storyboard.addedInformation: The land would become a modern visitor site.

image.subject: a patch of raw dark earth in an overgrown yard, with an old weathered grave marker half sunk in the soil under a grey sky

storyboard.claim: Digging would bring up the family's buried dead from three centuries.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dark disturbed soil and an old grave marker in the yard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains what the digging would reveal.
storyboard.addedInformation: The family's dead are buried in the grounds.

image.subject: a heavy chestnut front door of an old timber house, bolted and chained shut, with a dim light behind a narrow window beside it

storyboard.claim: The estate is under siege, so the people inside take drastic measures.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A bolted chestnut door and a dim window, the house shut against outsiders.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the threat into a state of siege.
storyboard.addedInformation: The inhabitants are desperate and shut inside.

image.subject: a seventeenth-century timber house with a heavy chestnut front door, seen from a gravel drive, and a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, standing on the step holding a suitcase

storyboard.claim: To understand Peton, follow Julia on her first day in the house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia arrives at the chestnut door of the timber house with a suitcase.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the siege to the person entering it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Julia has just arrived at the estate.

image.subject: a frail elderly man in a worn work coat, bent with effort, holding open a heavy chestnut door while a woman in plain modern clothes steps into a dim entrance hall

storyboard.claim: Mick, a frail old groundskeeper, opens the door for Julia with great effort.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An old man straining to hold the heavy door open for Julia.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Julia is now at the door, so the scene steps inside.
storyboard.addedInformation: Mick is the frail elderly groundskeeper.

storyboard.claim: Mick is very old.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text card only.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A quick aside about the groundskeeper.
storyboard.addedInformation: Mick is frail and very old.

image.subject: a dim second-floor hallway of a timber house, low ceiling, one old lamp, a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, stopped dead mid-step

storyboard.claim: The air is stale and the hallway is dim; Julia stops dead.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia freezes in a dim upstairs hallway.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Julia is inside and now stops in the hall.
storyboard.addedInformation: The upstairs hall is dim and stale.

image.subject: a steep wooden staircase rising into darkness toward an attic hatch, seen from the hallway, with a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, staring up from its foot

storyboard.claim: Julia stares at the wooden staircase to the attic and sees that it is wrong.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia at the foot of a steep staircase looking up into the attic dark.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Julia's stop becomes a specific object: the staircase.
storyboard.addedInformation: The staircase leads up to the attic.

image.subject: a close-up of a dark wooden staircase where each tread is a different height, the steps zigzagging left and right, shot from a low angle

storyboard.claim: Each side of the stairs alternates in height.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A close-up of uneven stair treads alternating left and right.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the wrongness Julia sees.
storyboard.addedInformation: The treads alternate in height side to side.

image.subject: a woman's feet in plain shoes, one on a low wooden step and the other on a higher separate block on the opposite side of a dark timber staircase

storyboard.claim: The left foot lands on one step and the right foot must land on a higher block.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two feet stepping on alternating heights of a staircase.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows how the uneven steps are walked.
storyboard.addedInformation: Walking the stairs means alternating up and down.

image.subject: a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, gripping a wooden newel post at the foot of a steep staircase, head tilted, looking unsteady

storyboard.claim: The stairs are dizzying and throw off balance at the bottom.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia steadying herself against the post at the stair foot.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the stair pattern to its effect on Julia.
storyboard.addedInformation: Julia feels dizzy standing at the bottom.

image.subject: a faded old photograph of a little girl with dark hair holding the hand of an older grey-haired woman in a dim hallway, the edges softened

storyboard.claim: Julia remembers holding her grandmother Letty's hand as a little girl.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A faded print of a girl holding an older woman's hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Julia's dizziness pulls up a childhood memory.
storyboard.addedInformation: The grandmother is named Letty.

image.subject: an older grey-haired woman in a dark dress, half her face in shadow, smiling a thin unsettling mischievous smile at the foot of a dark staircase

storyboard.claim: Letty smiles a deeply unsettling, mischievous smile.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Letty's face in half shadow, smiling thinly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The memory now shows Letty.
storyboard.addedInformation: Letty's smile is unsettling.

storyboard.claim: Letty says the stairs are witches' stairs, a family legend.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text card only.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The smile becomes the legend she tells.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stairs are called witches' stairs in the family lore.

image.subject: a dark timber staircase with alternating treads, a row of iron nails studding the bottom step in a deliberate pattern, seen from the landing

storyboard.claim: The treads were built to trip up the supernatural, which cannot climb irregular stairs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Irregular treads and a row of nails on the bottom step.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the legend's purpose to the stairs.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stairs were meant as a supernatural trap.

image.subject: a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, turning her head sharply over one shoulder toward a dark staircase, a visible shiver in her posture

storyboard.claim: The image makes the hair on Julia's neck stand straight up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia turns sharply toward the stairs, tense.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The legend hits Julia physically.
storyboard.addedInformation: Julia is spooked by the legend.

image.subject: a seventeenth-century timber house at night with its shutters barred and an iron bear door knocker on the heavy chestnut door

storyboard.claim: The house is framed from page one as an active battleground against the supernatural.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The timber house at night, barred shutters, iron bear knocker on the door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Widens the legend from the stairs to the whole house.
storyboard.addedInformation: The house is a shield against the supernatural.

image.subject: a row of restored colonial houses on a quiet village street, steep roofs and small-paned windows, a small historic sign on a post

storyboard.claim: Architectural quirks we romanticize are often physical traces of a society's paranoia.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Restored colonial houses on a quiet village street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from one house to the wider idea of old buildings.
storyboard.addedInformation: Old architecture can hide fear.

image.subject: visitors on a weekend tour of a preserved colonial house, a couple in casual clothes admiring a sharp-angled timber gable and a low leaded window

storyboard.claim: A preserved colonial home on a tour with its strange sharp angles.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tourists looking up at a sharp-angled timber gable.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings the reader into the visitor's view.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tour is a weekend activity.

image.subject: a low timber ceiling with a heavy iron-barred window letting in grey light, a plain empty colonial room with old wooden floorboards

storyboard.claim: The deliberately low ceilings and heavy iron windows look quaint to us.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Low beams and an iron-barred window in an empty room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The tour room shows the quaint details.
storyboard.addedInformation: Low ceilings and iron windows were deliberate.

storyboard.claim: The architecture is fossilized fear.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text card only.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The quaint details become a verdict.
storyboard.addedInformation: Old buildings preserve the fear that built them.

image.subject: a staircase of pale oak and pine treads leading up into an attic, with a carved protective symbol cut into the wall above the door

storyboard.claim: The family turned the staircase into a magical ward against the devil in the attic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Pale oak stairs rising to the attic, a carved symbol above the door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The fear becomes a family myth about the stairs.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stairs are a spell to keep the devil in the attic.

image.subject: a man in his forties, neat build, short hair, tweed jacket, polite but intense, leaning back in a diner booth and shrugging

storyboard.claim: Henry, the museum curator, bursts the supernatural bubble in a mundane way.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Henry shrugs back in a diner booth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the myth to the man who debunks it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Henry is a museum curator.

image.subject: a retro diner booth with a black and white checkered floor, a plate of cheeseburgers and fries on the table, a man in his forties with a tweed jacket and a woman in her thirties with shoulder-length dark hair and plain modern clothes sitting across from each other

storyboard.claim: Henry takes Julia to a classic retro diner in town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Henry and Julia in a diner booth with cheeseburgers and fries.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets the place for the debunking.
storyboard.addedInformation: They eat greasy cheeseburgers and fries in the diner.

image.subject: a man in his forties, neat build, short hair, tweed jacket, polite but intense, laughing softly over a tall milkshake glass in a diner booth, a woman in plain modern clothes leaning in with a serious look

storyboard.claim: Julia brings up the witch's stairs and Henry chuckles into his milkshake.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Henry chuckling over a milkshake while Julia leans in seriously.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The same booth, now the legend is raised.
storyboard.addedInformation: Henry finds the legend amusing.

storyboard.claim: Henry declares the witches' stairs a complete myth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text card only.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The laugh becomes a verdict.
storyboard.addedInformation: Henry rejects the supernatural explanation outright.

image.subject: a sepia architectural drawing of a narrow timber staircase fitted into a cramped hallway, with measurement lines and notes, laid out on a museum table

storyboard.claim: Alternating treads were a practical design that saved horizontal space in narrow hallways.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sepia plan of a narrow staircase in a cramped hallway.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Henry's myth-busting becomes a drawing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The design saved room where a standard staircase would not fit.

left.label: WITCHES' WARD
left.subject: a dark attic doorway at the top of a staircase, a carved protective symbol above it, a single candle in the dark

right.label: SPACE SAVER
right.subject: a plain sepia drawing of a narrow timber staircase on a museum table

storyboard.claim: Henry replaces the supernatural lore with cold, pragmatic architectural utility.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Left: a candlelit attic door with a ward. Right: a plain staircase drawing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The drawing turns into a contrast.
storyboard.addedInformation: The supernatural explanation is replaced by practical design.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns Ethel's threat into a picture of the ghost she invokes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the supernatural story as a tool the aunt is using.

storyboard.claim: A ghost story is being used as security for a crime scene.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The punchline set as text on screen, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the ghost image into a joke about protection.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the ghost story as a crime-scene defence.

storyboard.claim: The host asks what this means for Julia.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The question set as text on screen, no picture.
storyboard.onScreenText: WHAT DOES THIS MEAN FOR JULIA?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from Ethel to Julia's choices.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the next stretch as a question about Julia's response.

image.subject: Julia, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, crouches over a pale pelvic bone in black dirt, one hand moving toward her coat pocket, the dark timber house behind her

storyboard.claim: Any normal person would call the police right away.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia crouched over the bone, her hand moving toward her coat pocket.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question by putting Julia back at the bone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her hand toward her pocket shows the obvious action she is considering.

storyboard.claim: She does not say it is her great-great grandmother from 1692.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The line set as text on a dark card, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the words Julia would not say about the bone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the family claim the reason she does not call.

image.subject: two raccoons at the edge of dark woods sniffing a shallow hole in the yard, a dim timber house far behind them

storyboard.claim: Julia would rather leave the bone for the raccoons than call the police.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two raccoons at the woods edge sniffing a shallow hole, the house dim behind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the joke into a picture, the raccoons being left to deal with it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the absurd choice the narration names.

image.subject: a heavy chestnut front door in a dim hallway with a candle in a wall sconce, no people

storyboard.claim: Henry Ziegler has already told Julia the rules of the trap.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Henry in a tweed jacket, polite but intense, beside the chestnut door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings in the museum man whose offer depends on the land.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives Henry his look and places him at the house.

image.subject: yellow police tape stretched across the heavy chestnut front door of a timber house at dusk, no figure

storyboard.claim: If police find remains, the whole property becomes a state crime scene.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Yellow police tape across the chestnut front door at dusk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows Henry's warning with what would happen if the police came.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the tape closing the house itself.

left.label: THE LAW
left.subject: a legal document with a red wax seal on a dark desk beside a closed leather book

right.label: THE MONEY
right.subject: a tall stack of gold coins on a dark wooden table, candlelit

storyboard.claim: Julia must weigh reporting the remains against the museum's millions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A legal seal on one side and a stack of coins on the other.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the crime-scene consequence into the choice she faces.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the two pulls, duty and money, as objects on each side.

image.subject: a low old bedroom with a narrow bed, a worn quilt, a window onto the dark grounds and an empty armchair by the fireplace, no figure

storyboard.claim: Her grandmother is 85, frail and confused, and her home is the emotional leverage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A narrow old bed and quilt in a low bedroom, empty chair by the fire.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves the choice to the grandmother's home.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the grandmother's home the place at stake.

image.subject: a timber house at night lit by harsh white floodlights, a yellow backhoe parked on the churned front lawn, no figure

storyboard.claim: A forensic dig with floodlights and backhoes would kill her grandmother.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Harsh floodlights on the house and a backhoe parked on the churned lawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows what the excavation the narration describes would look like.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the cost of digging visible on the grandmother's house.

image.subject: a pale bone wrapped in cloth being set back into a hole, the dark earth half-filled around it, the timber house in the background, no figure

storyboard.claim: Julia chooses the estate's financial safety over the truth of the bones.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cloth-wrapped bone lowered back into a hole, the soil half-filled.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the choice into the act of putting the bones back.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the compromise as a reburial.

storyboard.claim: The house makes you an accomplice to its crimes just by living there.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The line set as text on screen, no picture.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE HOUSE MAKES YOU AN ACCOMPLICE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the chunk on the complicity the reburial made concrete.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the chunk's verdict on the house and the people who live in it.

image.subject: Julia, a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, kneeling at dusk in a backyard and pushing loose dark earth back into a hole with both hands

storyboard.claim: The house makes Julia bury the truth for love and money.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia refilling the hole she was meant to dig up
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the moral trap: she has chosen the estate's safety over the bones.
storyboard.addedInformation: She is the one covering the grave again, not a ghost.

image.subject: a seventeenth-century timber house, not a person, its heavy chestnut front door shut and its windows warmly lit against a dark evening

storyboard.claim: The house demands complicity to keep up its respectable face.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the handsome timber house presenting a calm front to the street
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from Julia's guilt to the house itself as the thing that demands it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The facade is shown as the lie that the bones sit behind.

storyboard.claim: Time inside Peton is used against the people who live there.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a dark title card with the words time and house set against each other
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from the complicit people to the way the house itself controls time.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the clock as the next object of attention.

image.subject: a tall antique grandfather clock of dark old wood standing in a dim candlelit living room, its brass pendulum visible through the glass door

storyboard.claim: The grandfather clock is the book's most unsettling object.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the tall clock standing in the candlelit room
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The time theme from the card now has a physical object.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the clock as the house's timekeeper.

image.subject: a close view of an old clock face with brass hands and a heavy brass pendulum blurred in mid-swing behind the glass

storyboard.claim: The pendulum swing is slow and hypnotic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the blurred brass pendulum swinging behind the clock face
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves closer to the clock to show the mechanism in motion.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock is as old as the house, shown through its face.

image.subject: Julia, a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, sitting bolt upright in an old bed in a dark bedroom, startled awake

storyboard.claim: Julia is woken in the middle of the night by the ticking echo.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia sitting up in bed in the dark, startled
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The ticking that filled the first floor has reached her bedroom.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows her awake and alone in the night.

storyboard.claim: A horrific moaning echoes down the second floor hallway.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card with the sound written out
storyboard.onScreenText: A HORRIFIC MOANING IN THE SECOND FLOOR HALL
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the ticking to a human sound in the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sound is named in words since it has no picture.

image.subject: a bedroom window seen from inside at night, moonlight through the glass, a smudged greasy handprint with unnaturally long thin fingers drying slowly down the outside of the pane

storyboard.claim: Julia finds a long greasy handprint on her window at night.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the smudged handprint with elongated fingers on the outside of the glass
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the moaning, the threat is now on her own window.
storyboard.addedInformation: The print is outside, so someone was on the grounds.

image.subject: Julia, a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, coming down a staircase in pale morning light, one hand on the banister

storyboard.claim: The next morning Julia goes downstairs and finds something wrong.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia descending the staircase in morning light
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the night at the window to the morning in the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: The reveal of the stopped clock waits downstairs.

image.subject: a close view of an antique clock face, its two brass hands frozen at 3:41, the heavy pendulum hanging motionless

storyboard.claim: The grandfather clock has stopped at 3:41.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the frozen hands at 3:41 on the clock face
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The clock from the earlier beats has now stopped.
storyboard.addedInformation: The time 3:41 is shown as the key number.

image.subject: a plain old wooden bedroom door in an ordinary house, a small brass lock and a worn key left in it, an everyday ordinary hallway behind

storyboard.claim: A haunting may be ordinary human malice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: an ordinary locked bedroom door with a key in it
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the clock, the narration moves to the explanation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ordinary door hints that the cause is a person, not a spirit.

storyboard.claim: Strange events make people think of ghosts first.
storyboard.concreteVisual: three short items listed as the strange events
storyboard.onScreenText: A SOUND / A DOOR / A STOPPED CLOCK
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists the three events just shown so the viewer can match them.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the idea that the mind reaches for ghosts.

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, standing in a dim doorway half lit by candle

storyboard.claim: A restless ghost is the easier explanation for the mind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a frightened woman in period dress in a candlelit doorway
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The list of events now gets a ghost to match.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ghost is shown as the story the mind wants to believe.

image.subject: a hand resting on the cold iron latch of a heavy dark wooden door inside an old house, a faint candle glow on the wood

storyboard.claim: A living person in the home is orchestrating the fear.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a hand on a latch of a door inside the house
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the ghost idea to the living person behind it.
storyboard.addedInformation: A real hand at a real door, not a spirit.

image.subject: a man in his fifties, heavy build, dark wool coat, white collar, stern face, standing in a shadowed candlelit hallway and looking straight ahead

storyboard.claim: Humans are more frightening than ghosts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a stern heavy man in a dark coat in a shadowed hall
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The living person is now given a face.
storyboard.addedInformation: The man is the real threat, not the ghost.

image.subject: a garden rake leaning against a dark wooden living room doorframe, muddy work overalls hanging on a hook beside it, a grandfather clock visible in the room beyond

storyboard.claim: The day after the window, the groundskeeper is in the living room with the clock.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a rake against the doorframe and muddy overalls on a hook, no person shown
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The orchestration now has a tool and a place.
storyboard.addedInformation: The rake and overalls point to the groundskeeper without drawing him.

storyboard.claim: The clock stops every night at exactly 3:41 a.m.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card with the claim written out
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The groundskeeper's claim turns the single stop into a nightly pattern.
storyboard.addedInformation: The nightly repeat is stated in words.

image.subject: an old clock case lying open on a cloth-covered table, its brass gears, springs and iron weights laid out in neat rows beside it

storyboard.claim: A repairman took the whole clock apart and found nothing wrong.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the clock mechanism laid out on cloth in rows
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the claim of the stop to the evidence of the taken-apart clock.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the mechanism that was supposedly inspected.

storyboard.claim: The repairman found nothing wrong with the gears or the weights.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card with the finding as the punchline
storyboard.onScreenText: NOTHING WRONG. NOTHING WRONG AT ALL.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Confirms the repair result as the twist before the watch.
storyboard.addedInformation: The finding is delivered as a bare punchline.

image.subject: a close-up of a silver analog wristwatch lying on a wooden table, its hands frozen at 3:41

storyboard.claim: A wristwatch also stops at 3:41 every night.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the silver watch with hands at 3:41 on a table
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The clock's stop is matched by a second stopped time piece.
storyboard.addedInformation: The second watch makes the stop look like a person's doing.

storyboard.claim: The stopping looks like a supernatural stop of time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card with the question of ghost or staging
storyboard.onScreenText: A SUPERNATURAL STOP OF TIME, OR A STAGE?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the watch, the question frames the two readings.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the book's reveal as a real choice.

storyboard.claim: 3:41 a.m. may be a historical marker in the family's past.
storyboard.concreteVisual: timeline card with 3:41 a.m. pointing back to a date
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the time into a link to the past.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects the stopped time to the 1692 story.

image.subject: a bare field at pale dawn, a charred wooden stake standing in grey ash, a dark timber village far off behind it, no person shown

storyboard.claim: Caroline Eldridge was burned at the stake at 3:41 a.m.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a charred stake in ash in a field at dawn
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The historical time now gets its place, with the violence softened to the aftermath.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stake and ash mark the 1692 death without showing it.

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, standing at a window at dawn with pale light on her face

storyboard.claim: The ghost of Caroline freezes time to make her family face her murder.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline at a window at dawn, frightened
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The historical marker now gets a ghost who would stop the clock.
storyboard.addedInformation: The Gothic theory is shown through her face.

storyboard.claim: The ghost theory is pure narrative misdirection.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card naming the theory as misdirection
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the Gothic ghost theory that the previous beat showed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the misdirection as the reason to reject the theory.

image.subject: Julia, a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, standing in a doorway with one hand over her mouth, shocked

storyboard.claim: Julia believed the ghost story as fully as the viewer did.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia in a doorway, hand over her mouth in shock
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the misdirection is named, Julia's reaction shows she fell for it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her shock marks the moment the story turns against her belief.

image.subject: an elderly woman in her eighties, thin, grey hair in a bun, dark cardigan, stern face, standing in a candlelit hallway in a dark robe, half turned toward the stairs

storyboard.claim: The haunting is a stage play run by the living residents.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ethel in a robe in a candlelit hall, half turned away
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The explanation of the staging now puts a performer on the set.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the performer who is playing Ethel in the house.

image.subject: a low old bedroom with a square trapdoor in the wooden floorboards lifted open onto a dark opening below

storyboard.claim: A hidden trapdoor in a bedroom gives the staging its route.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the square trapdoor lifted open in the bedroom floor
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The stage play now has its hidden exit.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the physical route the staging takes through the house.

image.subject: a narrow wooden ladder rising through a dark square hole in a low attic ceiling, old timber beams overhead, a candle on the floor below

storyboard.claim: A seventeenth-century trapdoor leads up through the walls into the attic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a ladder going up through the hole into the dark attic
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The trapdoor from the bedroom now connects to the attic above.
storyboard.addedInformation: The passage through the walls is made visible as a ladder.

storyboard.claim: The narrator asks how the haunting is actually carried out.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card with the logistics question
storyboard.onScreenText: HOW DO THEY FAKE A HAUNTING?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the attic passage, the question asks for the method step by step.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the next beats as the answer to the method.

image.subject: a rough hand gripping a heavy brass pendulum to stop it swinging, inside an open clock case in a dim candlelit room

storyboard.claim: The pendulum of the grandfather clock is jammed to stop it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a hand holding the pendulum still inside the clock case
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The method now shows how the clock was stopped.
storyboard.addedInformation: A hand on the pendulum shows the act, not the person.

image.subject: a close-up of a finger pulling out the small crown of a silver wristwatch, the watch lying on a wooden table

storyboard.claim: The wristwatch is stopped by pulling out its crown.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a finger pulling the crown of the silver watch
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The clock method is matched by the watch method.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows how a wristwatch is stopped by hand.

image.subject: a bedroom window seen from the dark garden at night, dewy glass with faint dark streaks running down the pane, no people

storyboard.claim: The living residents move through the hidden halls and drag hands down the windows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: dewy window streaked by downward handprints seen from outside
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the handprint, now seen from outside by the one who made it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows that the saboteurs are outside the glass too.

image.subject: an open old household ledger on a dark wooden table, handwritten columns of names and dates, a candle beside it

storyboard.claim: The haunting aims to scare Julia off so she cannot persuade Letty to sell to the museum.
storyboard.concreteVisual: an open household ledger with handwritten columns beside a candle
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The motive is set out, with the house's own records as the lever.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ledger points to the house's records as the motive for the sale.

storyboard.claim: They gaslight a vulnerable young woman with her family's ghost story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card naming the gaslighting
storyboard.onScreenText: GASLIGHTING A VULNERABLE YOUNG WOMAN WITH HER OWN FAMILY GHOST STORY
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The motive is now named as cruelty toward Julia.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the cruelty into words.

image.subject: the heavy chestnut front door of an old timber house, shut tight, with an iron bear-shaped knocker fixed to the wood

storyboard.claim: Peton's history is used as a weapon to keep physical control of the house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the shut front door with the iron bear knocker
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the cruelty to the house itself as the tool.
storyboard.addedInformation: The iron knocker stands for the house as a shield.

image.subject: a row of old framed family portraits on a dark wall, the faces hidden in shadow, a single candle lighting the frames

storyboard.claim: The estate breeds a toxic madness in its inhabitants.
storyboard.concreteVisual: old family portraits with their faces in shadow
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the weapon of history to the people it turns mad.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shadowed family faces show the madness inherited.

storyboard.claim: The inhabitants will do anything, including psychological torture, to keep the house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card stating the willingness to do anything
storyboard.onScreenText: THEY WILL DO ANYTHING TO KEEP THE HOUSE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the madness into the price of staying.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the stake of keeping the house in words.

image.subject: a brass house key and a folded old deed lying on a dark wooden table beside a few worn coins

storyboard.claim: The most shocking inheritance in the modern timeline is the theft.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a brass key, a folded deed and worn coins on a table
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the madness to the inheritance that carries it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Key, deed and coins name the inheritance as property.

image.subject: a single flashlight beam cutting through pitch-dark backyard grass, black trees around it and no other light

storyboard.claim: The modern timeline reaches its climax, a mind bender.
storyboard.concreteVisual: one flashlight beam through the black backyard
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The inheritance leads into the yard where the climax happens.
storyboard.addedInformation: The flashlight beam sets the scene for the next beats.

image.subject: Julia: a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, standing alone in a pitch-black yard at night, the timber walls of an old house behind her, looking off into the dark

storyboard.claim: Julia is alone and terrified in the dark yard, searching for the woman she believes is her great-aunt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia small in a black yard, the house dark behind her, her face turned toward the unseen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the scene in the present-day yard, after the previous story left the 1970s-era claims behind.
storyboard.addedInformation: The yard is pitch black and Julia is alone, so the danger is the dark itself.

image.subject: Ethel: an elderly woman in her eighties, thin, grey hair in a bun, dark cardigan, stern face, holding a heavy flashlight up at night in a dark yard so its beam lights her face

storyboard.claim: A woman with a heavy flashlight approaches, and the light on her face is about to reveal she is not who Julia thought.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An elderly stern face lit hard by a flashlight beam in the dark yard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Julia is waiting in the yard; now the figure she was searching for steps into the light.
storyboard.addedInformation: The light is the moment of recognition, and the face shown is the one Julia expected: Ethel's.

image.subject: Celia: a woman in her seventies, composed, grey-streaked hair, cardigan, cold expression, standing in the dark yard with a flashlight at her side, a faint smile that does not reach her eyes

storyboard.claim: The woman in the light is not Ethel but Celia Kain, the impostor, who shows no remorse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Celia's composed, cold face in the flashlight beam; the same yard, a different woman.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The flashlight face from the last beat is revealed as someone else.
storyboard.addedInformation: The impostor has a name, Celia Kain, and she is calm rather than afraid.

image.subject: The seventeenth-century timber house Peton at night, a long dark wall with a single lit upstairs window, a gravel drive in front, no people visible

storyboard.claim: Over fifty years ago, Celia worked as a servant at Peton and helped the real Ethel give birth at home in secret.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Peton at night with one upstairs window lit, the house holding the secret.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Celia's identity is named; now the story goes back to the house where it began.
storyboard.addedInformation: The 1970s secret happened inside this same house, not somewhere else.

image.subject: A low old bedroom at night lit by one candle on a table, an old wooden bed with rumpled white sheets, the window dark behind it, no one in the room

storyboard.claim: The birth happened secretly in a bedroom at Peton, a huge scandal if it had been known.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty bed in a candlelit bedroom, the sheets still disturbed after a birth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the house exterior to the room inside where the secret took place.
storyboard.addedInformation: The scene is a bedroom at night with a single candle, and it is empty: the people are only implied.

image.subject: A plump white down pillow lying on an old bed in a dim bedroom, its shape pressed flat, one candle burnt low on the nightstand, no people

storyboard.claim: Celia smothered the real Ethel with a down pillow while she was weak after giving birth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A pressed-flat white down pillow on an old bed, the only sign of the act.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Still in the same bedroom from the birth; the object now carries the murder.
storyboard.addedInformation: The weapon is a down pillow, an ordinary household object, which makes the act feel domestic.

image.subject: An old worn passport and a folded driver's license lying on a wooden table beside a neatly folded dark dress and a leather handbag, in a candlelit room

storyboard.claim: Celia took Ethel's passport, driver's license, clothes and whole life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ethel's papers and clothes laid out on a table, now belonging to someone else.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the murder, the objects of the dead woman are taken, following the pillow beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Identity is shown as paper and clothing, the things a person owns to be themselves.

image.subject: A dark wool cardigan hanging on a wooden peg beside an old front door inside a timber house, the room dim, no one present

storyboard.claim: Celia lived at Peton for fifty years pretending to be Ethel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ethel's cardigan waiting on its peg, a life worn in one house for decades.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The stolen clothes from the last beat are now hung up in the house, in daily use.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fifty years show as routine: a coat on a peg, lived in every day.

image.subject: A plain modern back door of a suburban house, closed, with a deadbolt and a welcome mat outside, a porch light on, no one in the frame

storyboard.claim: The ultimate home invasion is not a thief at the back door; it is someone taking your identity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A closed, ordinary back door: the house as it looks from outside, safe on the surface.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the 1970s house to the viewer's own home, to set up the comparison.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ordinary back door is the contrast: the threat is not a break-in but an identity theft.

image.subject: Celia: a woman in her seventies, composed, grey-streaked hair, cardigan, cold expression, standing in a dim hallway of an old timber house looking at her reflection in a tall old mirror

storyboard.claim: A parasite steals your identity and roots itself so deeply into your home that it becomes you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Celia in the hallway mirror, her reflection the only figure, as if it were Ethel's.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The back-door contrast gives way to the person who has moved in and taken over the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: The reflection makes the idea of becoming someone else visible.

storyboard.claim: The parasite roots itself so deeply that it takes over the family itself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Pure banter in the narration: no single picture would add to the claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the same idea from the mirror beat without a new picture.
storyboard.addedInformation: The point is the depth of the takeover, carried by the words alone.

image.subject: The heavy chestnut front door of a seventeenth-century timber house with an old iron bear-head door knocker, the door shut, a stone step worn smooth

storyboard.claim: The house does not care who occupies it or whose name is on the deed, as long as the blood sacrifices are kept.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The chestnut door and iron bear knocker: the house as a guardian that keeps its own.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the person inside the house to the house itself, the door that keeps occupants in.
storyboard.addedInformation: The iron bear knocker is the house's protector, and the closed door is its barrier.

image.subject: A dusty oval family portrait hanging in a dim wooden hallway, the painted faces dark with age, the frame cracked

storyboard.claim: The clues were there the whole time, in the family's own past.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An old family portrait in a hallway, the past watching from the wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the house's protection to the family history it hides, shown as an old portrait.
storyboard.addedInformation: The family is shown as a line of faces that has always been in the house.

image.subject: A low old bedroom with an empty armchair by the window, a folded wool shawl over its arm, a window onto dark grounds, no one in the chair

storyboard.claim: Grandmother Letty, supposedly slipping into dementia, keeps calling Julia by the wrong name, Celia.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty armchair by the window, the room where the old woman's mind was wandering.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the clues in the family past to the room where Letty said the name.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chair is empty, so the picture points at the absent woman rather than a face.

storyboard.claim: Everyone brushes it off as dementia, but it was not dementia at all.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text card: the reversal lands on its own words.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the dementia from the last beat into its opposite.
storyboard.addedInformation: The reversal is the point: the same words now mean the truth.

image.subject: Caroline: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, standing against a plain timber wall in a dim room

storyboard.claim: Letty sees a young woman in her house and links her to the last young woman who tore the family apart: Caroline.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline's frightened face in the 1692 dress, the link between two centuries.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Letty's confusion to the 1692 woman she was actually seeing.
